Capability metadata for a time-series foundation model

Source: R/capabilities.R
new_zuk_capabilities.Rd

A zuk_capabilities object is a small record describing what a model can and cannot do. It is attached to every model returned by zuk_pretrained() and is used for pre-flight validation: a fit or forecast call is rejected with an informative error before any tensor work if the request exceeds the model's declared capabilities.

new_zuk_capabilities(
  architecture,
  max_context,
  max_horizon = Inf,
  quantiles = c("native", "none"),
  quantile_levels = NULL,
  multivariate = FALSE,
  samples = FALSE,
  past_covariates = FALSE,
  future_covariates = FALSE,
  static_covariates = FALSE,
  fine_tunable = FALSE,
  license = NA_character_
)

Arguments

architecture

Character scalar, the architecture key (e.g. "ttm").

max_context

Integer, the maximum supported context length.

max_horizon

Numeric scalar, the maximum supported forecast horizon, or Inf when the architecture has no smaller declared limit.

quantiles

One of "native" (the model emits quantiles directly) or "none".

quantile_levels

Numeric vector of quantile levels the checkpoint can emit, or NULL when a native-quantile architecture accepts arbitrary levels.

multivariate, past_covariates, future_covariates

Grouped-input channels. They may be TRUE only for an architecture written against contract 1.1 or later; new_zuk_model() refuses the combination otherwise. See ?zuk-architecture-contract.

samples, static_covariates, fine_tunable

Reserved logical fields. They must remain FALSE: no contract version has an execution channel for those inputs or outputs, and declaring one would describe behaviour that cannot run.

license

Character scalar, the SPDX identifier of the weight licence.

Value

A zuk_capabilities object.

Examples

new_zuk_capabilities("demo", max_context = 512L)
#> <zuk_capabilities>
#>   architecture:      demo
#>   max_context:       512        max_horizon: Inf
#>   quantiles:         native        levels: arbitrary
#>   multivariate:      FALSE        samples:   FALSE
#>   past_covariates:   FALSE        future_covariates: FALSE
#>   static_covariates: FALSE        fine_tunable: FALSE
#>   license:           NA
#> 

# A checkpoint with fixed trained quantile levels declares them, and the
# engine then refuses any other level before running the forward pass.
new_zuk_capabilities(
  "demo",
  max_context = 512L,
  max_horizon = 64,
  quantile_levels = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9),
  license = "Apache-2.0"
)
#> <zuk_capabilities>
#>   architecture:      demo
#>   max_context:       512        max_horizon: 64
#>   quantiles:         native        levels: 0.1, 0.5, 0.9
#>   multivariate:      FALSE        samples:   FALSE
#>   past_covariates:   FALSE        future_covariates: FALSE
#>   static_covariates: FALSE        fine_tunable: FALSE
#>   license:           Apache-2.0
#>
